docs.title: Contact Support
docs.text:
Can't find your answer above? We're here to help.

First, try searching the Help Center — most questions are answered in a guide, and it's the fastest way to get unstuck.

Still need a hand? Reach us whichever way is easiest:

How to reach us Details 📝 Submit a request Open our online form — send us the details and we'll take it from there. ✉️ Email support@blossom.ag 📞 Call 715-710-1132 — press 1 for Tech Support 📱 Text Text us at 715-710-1132 💬 Live chat Coming soon — chat with us during support hours.

Support hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM CT

What to expect: We'll confirm we've received your request within 1 business day and let you know the next steps. If something needs our engineering team, we'll keep you posted as it moves.

Have an idea to make Blossom better? We'd love to hear it — send it our way and we'll pass it along to the product team.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text: Quick answers to the questions growers ask most. Each links to the full page.

docs.title: Getting around
docs.text:
How do I change the year I'm looking at? Use the year selector at the bottom-left, beside your farm name. Most screens — beds, applications, harvest, water, scouting — are tied to the selected season. See Setting your farm up for what follows the year and what doesn't.

A menu item I expected isn't in the sidebar. Sidebar items are granted by your role, so a missing one is usually a permission rather than a missing feature. See Roles.

docs.title: Beds
docs.text:
I moved to a new year and my beds are gone. Beds belong to a season. On an empty year, Beds offers New bed with three routes: Add bed manually, Copy from another year, or Import from CSV. Copying last season is usually what you want. See Managing Your Beds.

How do I group beds into blocks or management units? They're tabs on the Beds screen — Blocks and Management Units, beside Beds and Vines. See Blocks & Management Units.

docs.title: Harvest
docs.text:
Harvest shows 0 barrels — where's my crop? Barrels come from deliveries, which you import from your handler. Open Harvest ▸ Deliveries ▸ Import deliveries. See Deliveries.

I entered a yield but it doesn't match my deliveries. A yield you type on the Harvest ▸ Yields tab overrides the imported delivery barrels for that bed. Use it to correct or fill gaps, not to double-count. See Yields.

docs.title: Pesticides & compliance
docs.text:
When can anyone go back into the bed? Open the application from the ledger. RESTRICTIONS FOR THIS MIX states the binding hold in plain words, and it is the longest REI in the tank — not the one you sprayed most of. See Pesticide posting & restricted-entry (REI) signs.

How do I print the posting sign for the field? Reports ▸ Pest Management ▸ Pesticide Application Posting, then choose the posting date. That's the sign. The Print the application record link on a ledger card gives you something different — the signed office copy. Both are explained on the same page, above.

Where is my Pesticide Use Report (PUR)? Reports ▸ Pest Management ▸ Pesticide Use Report. See Submitting your PUR.

How do I send my pesticide use to Ocean Spray? Use the PUR Transfer tab on the Applications screen. See PUR Transfer — Ocean Spray & Agrian.

I'm recording a spray that hasn't happened yet. Switch Completed off — on the Log pesticide screen it arrives switched on. Check Method too; it arrives set to GROUND. See Recording a Pesticide Application.

docs.title: Scouting
docs.text:
Where do scout groups come from? Settings ▸ Scout Groups — you name the scouting company and pick the beds it covers. See Scouts & scout groups.

Why does a pest count look high on the trends graph? Check whether the beds behind it were actually swept. The average only counts what was recorded — and a recorded 0 pulls it down while a blank is ignored. See Logging a Scouting Report.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: How do I add someone to my farm? Settings ▸ Users, then Add user or Invite. See Adding Users to Your Farm.

docs.title: Data in & out
docs.text:
Can I bulk-import my existing records? Beds, harvest deliveries and lab test results you can import yourself. Anything larger — historical seasons, records from another system — Blossom does for you. See Importing & exporting your data.

Can I export to Excel or CSV? Not in bulk. Use the Reports section to print or save. If you need another format, ask Blossom.

Don't see your question? Contact Support.

docs.title: Adding Users to Your Farm
docs.text:
Settings & account ▸ Access ▸ Users.

Each person shows their name, username, email, when they were last seen, and their role. Search by name, username or email.

docs.title: Two ways to add someone
docs.text:
• Invite — send an invitation so they set their own password and sign in.
  • Add user — create the account yourself.

Either way you give them a role, which decides what they can see and do.

Invite rather than add, where you can

An invited user sets their own password, so nobody else ever knows it. It also means the account is genuinely theirs, which is what makes the "entered by" on every record worth anything.

docs.title: Last seen tells you what's really being used
docs.text:
The Last seen column is quietly useful: Today, Yesterday, Never. An account that has never been used is either somebody who needs help getting started, or a login nobody needs.

Mechanics and scouts are separate lists

People who service machines are managed under Maintenance ▸ Mechanics, and scouting parties under Scout groups. Only people who sign in to Blossom belong here.

docs.title: Changing Farm Settings
docs.text: Settings that affect the whole farm, not just you. Settings & account ▸ Farm ▸ Farm.

docs.title: Where you are
docs.text:
• Growing region — WI, NJ, MA, OR, WA, BC, QC, ON, AT or CH.
  • Farm address — street, city, state and ZIP.

The address drives your weather

Blossom spells this out: the forecast and rainfall readings "are drawn for this address when no bed on the map carries a boundary." If Weather is showing the wrong town, this is why — fill the address in, or map your beds.

docs.title: What gets tracked
docs.text:
• Default sanding depth (in) — the depth a new sanding event starts at.
  • Track maintenance costs — turn this on and maintenance records gain an estimated cost field. With it off, the field simply isn't there.
  • Water tracking methods — Use bed floods (inches/acre) and Use pump events (gallons/min). Switch on whichever way you actually measure water.

docs.title: How lists behave
docs.text:
• Collapse lists on start — with Enable all and Disable all to set every list at once.
  • List sort order — per record type, choose Latest first or Earliest first: fertilizer applications, flooding events, harvest, and the rest.

Sort order is worth five minutes

Most people want the newest record first while a season is running. Setting it once, per list, saves a small irritation every single time you open one.

docs.title: Adding a Handler Contract
docs.text:
A handler contract records who you're delivering to, for which crop year, and how much you've committed.

Settings & account ▸ Farm ▸ Handler Contracts.

  1. Open Handler Contracts.
  2. Tap Add contract.
  3. Record the handler, the crop year and the pounds committed.

Contracts are per season

A new year starts empty — "No contracts recorded for 2026." Contracts belong to a crop year, so they're entered again each season rather than carried across.

docs.title: Why it matters beyond paperwork
docs.text:
Your contract is what your delivery data is measured against. With it recorded, Harvest can show how the season is tracking toward what you committed, rather than just counting barrels.

If you deliver to Ocean Spray, the contract number also appears when you match beds for PUR Transfer.

docs.title: Importing your data
docs.text:
Some records you can bring in yourself; a whole farm's history is a job for the Blossom team, so it lands correctly.

For anything bigger, Blossom does it for you

Email support@blossom.ag or call 715-710-1132 and say what you'd like to import — see Contact us.

What you can import yourself

A few specific records have a built-in Import button for the file your handler or lab sends:

  • Beds — on an empty season, New bed offers Add bed manually, Copy from another year or Import from CSV. Copying last season is usually what you want in January — see Managing Your Beds.
  • Harvest deliveries — see Deliveries
  • Soil tests and Tissue tests — see Importing test results

Anything beyond these — historical seasons, records from another system — is the bigger job Blossom handles for you.

docs.title: Exporting your data
docs.text:
To get information out of Blossom, use the Reports section — reports are grouped by area (Beds, Nutrient Management, Pest Management, Harvest, and more) and can be printed or saved. See Running reports.

There is no bulk CSV export. If you need your data in another format, Blossom can help.

Blossom does this for you

Email support@blossom.ag or call 715-710-1132 — see Contact us.

docs.title: Licensed applicators
docs.text: Everyone who applies pesticide on your farm, with their certification.

docs.title: The roster
docs.text:
Each applicator shows their name, certification number (for example MA-18255) and when it expires. Search by name, company or certification number.

Tap Add Applicator to add someone.

Watch for 'No expiry on file'

An applicator with no expiry recorded shows Expires — Not on file. That isn't the same as a current certification; it means nobody has entered one. Since an expired licence is a compliance problem, this is worth filling in before an inspector asks rather than after.

docs.title: The day view
docs.text:
The page opens on a date, with Today beside it and the option to show the work orders assigned on this day. Each applicator has Print work orders for [name] — which is how you hand someone their day on paper.

This is the applicator's morning

Pick the date, print each applicator's orders, and the crew leaves with what they need. The same information is what they'd see in their own login, under Applications.

docs.text:

  • Submitting your PUR — where their name appears in the record.

docs.title: Products — pesticides, fertilizers & adjuvants
docs.text:
Every product you can pick when recording an application comes from here.

Tap Settings & account (bottom-left) → Reference → Products. Three tabs sit across the top: Pesticides, Fertilizers and Adjuvants.

Moved in V2

In the old Blossom the fertilizer list lived under Nutrients. It's now part of Settings ▸ Reference, alongside varieties, pests and chemical rules.

docs.title: Two kinds of product on every tab
docs.text:
Each list mixes two things, and the difference matters:

  • The shared catalog — the registered pesticide catalog and the shared fertilizer catalog are the same for every farm, and read-only here. You can use these products but not change them.
  • Your farm's own products — anything your farm adds belongs to your farm, and your farm can edit or retire it.

Product missing from the catalog?

You can add it yourself — there's an Add pesticide button on the Pesticides tab and Add fertilizer on Fertilizers. This is a change from the old Blossom, where a missing pesticide meant contacting support.

docs.title: Finding a product
docs.text: Use Search products by name, brand or active ingredient, or Filter to narrow the list. Searching by active ingredient is the quickest way to find alternatives to a product you can't get hold of.

docs.title: Adding a fertilizer
docs.text:
1. Open the Fertilizers tab.
  2. Tap Add fertilizer.
  3. Enter the name, brand and units.
  4. Enter the nutrient analysis — Nitrogen, P₂O₅, K₂O, plus any of calcium, magnesium, sulfur, copper, iron, manganese, molybdenum, zinc and boron.
  5. Save.

Get the analysis right

The percentages you enter here are what Blossom multiplies by your application rates to work out what actually went on each bed. An analysis typed wrong quietly produces wrong nutrient reports all season.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
A role is a named set of permissions. Every user has one, and it decides both what they can do and what they even see.

Settings & account ▸ Access ▸ Roles.

docs.title: The roles that ship with Blossom
docs.text:
Fifteen roles come ready to use, from Read-only Viewer through job-shaped ones — Accountant, Agronomist, Applicator, Crew Lead, Equipment Foreman, Field Applicator, Foreman, Manager, Mechanic, Office Manager, Operator, Shop Foreman — up to Farm admin and Organization Admin.

The list shows how many permissions each role holds and how many people are using it.

docs.title: How permissions are built
docs.text:
Pick a role and its permissions appear grouped by feature — Beds, Map, Calendar, Nutrient Applications, Soil & Tissue Tests, Pesticide Applications, Scouting Reports, Traps, Equipment, Maintenance and the rest.

Each feature has its own switches: view, record, edit, delete, and others specific to it.

'Side Bar View' is the one that surprises people

Most features also carry a Side Bar View permission, and that is literally what puts the item in the sidebar. A role can hold every permission for a feature and still not see it in the menu if Side Bar View is off — the person will tell you the feature is "missing" when it's simply not drawn.

Diagnosing "I can't find it"

When somebody says a menu item has disappeared, check their role's Side Bar View for that feature before anything else. It's the most common explanation, and it looks nothing like a permissions error from their side.

docs.title: Data restrictions
docs.text: Roles can also carry data restrictions — No Cost Metrics and No Revenue Metrics — for people who should see the work but not the money.

docs.title: Work order types
docs.text: Which kinds of work order this farm writes. Settings & account ▸ Farm ▸ Work Orders.

docs.title: The five types
docs.text:
Pesticide · Nutrient · Maintenance · Water · Vines.

Switch a type off and it's no longer offered when someone writes a new order.

Turning a type off is safe

Blossom is explicit: "a type that is off is not offered on the add page; orders already filed under it are untouched and still appear on the worklist." You're changing what can be created, not hiding history.

docs.title: Defaults for a new order
docs.text:
• New orders open on — which type a new order starts as. Set it to whatever your farm writes most, and most orders need one less tap.
  • Dates on a new order — both dates start on today, "since orders are usually entered the day they are requested." Turn one off if that doesn't match how you work.

Match this to the farm you actually are

A farm that never writes vine work orders shouldn't be offered them, and a farm that mostly writes maintenance orders shouldn't start every order as a pesticide one. Two minutes here removes a small friction from every order afterwards.

docs.title: Your account
docs.text: Everything under You in settings affects you alone, not the farm.

docs.title: Profile
docs.text: Settings & account ▸ Profile holds your first and last name, username and email, with Edit profile and Change password beside them.

docs.title: Changing your password
docs.text:
1. Open Settings & account ▸ Profile.
  2. Tap Change password.
  3. Enter your current password, then the new one twice.

Each person needs their own login

Blossom records who entered what — every application, scouting report and service record carries a name. Sharing one login makes that record meaningless, and it's the main reason to give people their own user account.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
Push Notifications can be enabled to receive maintenance reminders — alerts for upcoming and overdue maintenance tasks. It starts disabled.

Worth turning on if you run the shop

This is the one notification Blossom sends, and it pairs with the Maintenance Due report. If nobody has it on, overdue services rely on somebody remembering to look.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text:
Choose System, Light or Dark.

This one is per device, not per account

Blossom says so plainly: "the choice is saved in this browser, so your phone and your desktop can differ — it is not part of your Blossom account." Set it on each device you use.

docs.title: Applications
docs.text:
Everything you put on a bed is recorded here — pesticides and nutrients together. Tap Applications in the sidebar.

This is the biggest change from the old Blossom

Sprays and fertilizer used to live in two different places: Pest Management for one, Nutrients for the other. In V2 they share one screen, and you filter to the kind you want.

docs.title: Finding your way around
docs.text:
The screen has two tabs:

  • Applications — the ledger of what's been applied.
  • PUR Transfer — sending pesticide use to Ocean Spray or Agrian.

On the Applications tab, two rows of filters narrow what you see:

Filter Options Kind All · Pesticide · Nutrients Status All · Requested · Approved · Completed

The status chips on the cards themselves read a little differently — Open, Awaiting approval, Completed — so don't expect the two lists to match word for word.

There's also a search box — search by product, target pest, bed or applicator — which is usually faster than filtering when you know what you're looking for.

docs.title: What a ledger entry shows
docs.text:
Each application in the list carries the date, the applicator, a kind chip (PESTICIDE or NUTRIENT), the products, and — for a spray — when its REI clears:

Weedar 64 · Provixo 480 SC · REI clears Wed, Sep 30 · Rate 7.82 fl oz/ac · Coverage 21.31 ac · Target Fireworm · Completed

A nutrient entry shows the same skeleton with a bed count and the analysis instead of a target: 5-10-25 · 7 Beds · Rate 294 lbs/ac · Coverage 25.82 ac · N / P₂O₅ / K₂O.

REI clearance is on the ledger itself

You don't have to open an application, or dig out the posting sheet, to find out when a bed comes back into play. The ledger says it on every row — and on the nearest ones it says it in plain words: REI clears today, REI clears tomorrow. A product with no interval on file reads REI unknown, which means go and read the label, not that there is no restriction.

docs.title: Work orders sit here too
docs.text:
Not every entry is something that has already happened. Work orders — jobs written down in advance — appear in the same list, dated by when they are due rather than when they were done:

Work order #1037 · Target September 11, 2026 · Products applied: Drexel Carbaryl 4L · Badge SC · … · 1 application · 18.47 ac · Open

They are worth understanding separately, because a work order is where Blossom works out the combined re-entry and harvest restrictions for a tank mix.

Work orders

docs.title: Recording something
docs.text:
Tap New application and you get four choices, not two — because you can either record what happened or order what should:

Log (it happened) Work order (it should happen) Pesticide Log pesticide New pesticide work order Nutrient Log nutrient application New nutrient work order

The two work order options are how a planned job gets onto the ledger — see Work orders.

The two Log options are below:

  • Pesticide application

    Products, adjuvants, method, beds, applicator, target pests and weather.

    Open

  • Nutrient application

    Fertilizer, rate, beds — and whether it counts toward nutrient management.

    Open

docs.text:

  • Pesticide posting & restricted-entry (REI) signs — the sheet you print for the field.
  • Products — the pesticides, fertilizers and adjuvants you can choose from.
  • Reports — your Pesticide Use Report and the nutrient summaries.

docs.title: Nutrient Applications
docs.text: Fertilizer goes in the same place as sprays now — the Applications screen, filtered to Nutrients.

docs.title: Recording an application
docs.text:
1. Tap Applications in the sidebar, then New application → Log nutrient application.
  2. Fill in WHEN & STATE:
    • Date — required.
    • Rate (per acre) — required.
    • Exclude from Nutrient Management — off by default, which is right for normal applications. Switch it on only when an application should not count toward your nutrient management totals.
    • Completed — ⚠️ off by default. Switch it on once the job is done, or the application stays open.
  3. Under BEDS, pick every bed that received it.
  4. Under PRODUCT, pick the fertilizer. Products are listed by analysis and brand — 0-0-50 Insight FS, 0-45-0 Triple Super Phosphate Bonide.
  5. EQUIPMENT is optional — the spreader or tank it went on.
  6. ADVANCED holds applicator, method, times and weather.
  7. Tap Log application — or Save & log another to start a second one with the form already open. Clear empties it.

This toggle works the opposite way to the pesticide form

Completed starts off here and on on the Log pesticide screen. Same word, same place, opposite default. A nutrient application saved without switching it on stays open; a pesticide application saved without switching it off is recorded as already done.

One rate for the whole application

Unlike a pesticide spray — where every product carries its own rate on every bed — a nutrient application has a single Rate (per acre) at the top, applied across all the beds you pick. One product, one rate.

Why the analysis matters

Because each product on your list carries its nutrient analysis, Blossom can work out the actual pounds of N, P and K that landed on each bed. That's what produces the nutrient summaries and the NRCS 590 reports — so an accurate product list is what makes the reports right.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Products — adding a fertilizer to your farm's list.
  • Blocks & management units — the groupings your nutrient reports are broken out by.
  • Reports — the nutrient summaries and NRCS 590 reports.

docs.title: Recording a Pesticide Application
docs.text: Record each spray once, and Blossom carries it through to your posting sheet and your Pesticide Use Report — so the care you take here is what makes reporting easy later.

docs.title: Opening the right screen
docs.text:
1. Tap Applications in the sidebar.
  2. Tap New application. Four choices appear:
    • Log pesticide — a spray that has happened (this page)
    • Log nutrient application — see Nutrient Applications
    • New pesticide work order — a spray planned for later
    • New nutrient work order
  3. Choose Log pesticide.

Logging versus ordering

Log records something that happened. New … work order writes down a job to be done, which someone completes later — see Work orders. Same products, different moment.

docs.title: How the screen is laid out
docs.text:
Two panels that work together.

On the left — the application itself:

  • Method — Air, Ground, Sprinklers or Wipe.
  • Target — the pest you sprayed for.
  • Date — required.
  • Completed — whether the job is done.
  • ADVANCED — times, weather and a note.
  • APPLICATIONS — starts empty and fills in as you build the spray.

On the right — three tabs you work through:

Tab What you pick Beds The beds sprayed, grouped by block with each bed's variety — A1 — Mullica Queen. All takes a whole block; there's also Select all, Filters and a search Products Grouped Fungicide · Herbicide · Insecticide · Plant growth regulator · Adjuvant, with a filter. Adjuvants live in this same list Applicator Who applied it

Each tab shows a running count once you've chosen — Beds · 1 bed, Products · 1 product.

Two fields arrive already filled in

Method loads set to GROUND, and Completed loads switched on. Both are right for the commonest case — a ground spray you have just finished — and neither announces itself. An aerial application saved without changing Method files as a ground application, which is a wrong compliance record. Check both before you save.

docs.title: Building the spray
docs.text:
1. On the Beds tab, pick every bed that was sprayed.
  2. On the Products tab, pick every product in the tank.

  3. Look at the APPLICATIONS panel on the left. Each product now appears as a card with a unit selector (fl oz/ac) and, under it, one row per bed:

    Abound · fl oz/ac · 1 bed └ A1 · Applicator · rate · fl oz

  4. Enter the rate for each row, and set the applicator if it differs.

  5. Fill in Method, Target and Date on the left, and open ADVANCED for start and end times, weather and notes.
  6. Tap Log pesticide — or Save & log another if more sprays went on the same day. Clear empties the form and starts over.

Rate is per product, per bed

This is why rate isn't a single box at the top. Three products across four beds gives you twelve rows, each with its own rate — which is what makes the quantities on your posting sheet and PUR come out right.

docs.title: The restrictions box updates as you work
docs.text:
As soon as there's a product in the mix, RESTRICTIONS FOR THIS MIX appears in the left panel and recalculates with every change:

Binding hold: REI 4 h — Abound · do not enter without PPE until — No PHI on file for this mix — check each product label before harvesting.

Watch it while you add products

Add a 48-hour product to a tank of 4-hour ones and the binding hold jumps to 48 hours in front of you — before you have committed to the mix. That is the moment to reconsider, not after the sprayer is empty. How this is worked out explains the rule; the label always governs.

docs.title: After you save
docs.text:
One accurate record feeds three things automatically:

  • The posting and the application record — see Pesticide posting & restricted-entry (REI) signs.
  • Your Pesticide Use Report — see Submitting your PUR.
  • Your Ocean Spray or Agrian transfer, if you deliver to them — see PUR Transfer.

Check the beds before you save

Make sure every bed you actually treated is selected. A missing bed is far harder to spot three months later at reporting time.

docs.title: Pesticide posting & restricted-entry (REI) signs
docs.text: After a spray the field needs a posting sheet showing the restricted-entry interval — how long before anyone may go back in. Blossom builds it from the applications you recorded, so the sheet matches the record.

docs.title: The quickest answer: open the application
docs.text:
You don't need to print anything to find out when a bed is safe to enter. Open any application from the ledger and it shows RESTRICTIONS FOR THIS MIX in plain words:

Binding hold: REI 12 h — Callisto · do not enter without PPE until Fri, May 29, 2026

Earliest harvest: Mon, Jul 13, 2026 — longest PHI is 45 d (Callisto).

Above it, each product in the TANK MIX is listed with its group, manufacturer, rate, the total mixed for the acreage — 18.1 fl oz/ac · 190.96 fl oz for 10.55 ac — and its own REI and PHI. Below it, every bed treated, with its variety and block.

This is the same calculation as a work order

A work order shows the identical box before the job; a completed application shows it after. Longest REI governs the whole treated area, longest PHI sets the earliest harvest, and the label always governs over both.

docs.title: Two different printouts — don't mix them up
docs.text:
Blossom prints two documents, for two different purposes. They look similar and are easy to confuse.

Posting Application record Purpose The sign for the field The office copy for your file Reach it from Reports ▸ Pest Management ▸ Pesticide Application Posting Print the application record on any ledger card Picks by Posting date One application Headed Pesticide Application RECORD OF APPLICATION — OFFICE COPY

docs.title: The posting — what goes on the gate
docs.text:
Open Reports ▸ Pest Management ▸ Pesticide Application Posting, choose the Posting date, and tap Print.

It carries:

  • The farm, and the date with the time window — September 25, 2026 5:30 am – 8:00 am
  • Restricted Entry — 24 hours, stated near the top
  • A Pesticides table: name, active ingredient, EPA #, rate, REI and PHI
  • The beds it applies to
  • Other Details — applied by (with certification number), method, target pests and weather conditions

docs.title: The application record — what goes in the file
docs.text:
Reached from the ledger, one application at a time. It repeats the same facts but adds the ones an auditor asks for:

  • Total applied per product as well as the rate per acre — 7.82 fl oz/ac · 166.64 fl oz
  • Beds treated with each bed's variety and acres, and a total
  • The work order it came from, if any
  • An Applicator signature and Date signed block
  • A record number in the footer — Record #126161

One is for the field, one is for the folder

If someone is about to walk into a bog, they need the posting. If you're answering a question months later about what went on where, you want the application record — it's the one with the signature line.

Rate is recorded per product, per bed

An application with three products across four beds holds twelve rates, not one. Blossom multiplies each by the acreage to give the total applied, which is the number that reaches both documents and your PUR — see Recording a Pesticide Application.

The posted REI is the longest one in the tank

Where an application mixes products, the sheet posts the longest REI, not each product's own. A tank with a 48-hour product and a 12-hour product posts 48 hours — the figure people re-enter on. The table below still lists each product's individual REI and PHI.

Record the time window, not just the date

REI runs from the end of application, and the sheet prints the window you recorded. An application with no times can only be posted from the date, which is coarser than the label requires and usually costs working hours.

docs.title: PUR Transfer — Ocean Spray & Agrian
docs.text:
If you deliver to Ocean Spray, or report through Agrian, you can send your pesticide-use data straight from Blossom instead of re-keying it.

Tap Applications in the sidebar, then the PUR Transfer tab. It has a tab for each destination: Ocean Spray and Agrian.

This is separate from your county PUR

PUR Transfer sends data to a handler or a reporting service. Your regulatory Pesticide Use Report is a different job — see Submitting your PUR.

docs.title: Ocean Spray
docs.text:
Ocean Spray transfer needs to be switched on for your account before it will work. If it isn't, the tab tells you so, and you'll need:

  • an active Ocean Spray grower contract
  • Ocean Spray API access enabled on your account
  • valid API credentials configured

Contact your administrator or your Ocean Spray representative to get that enabled.

docs.title: Matching your beds (one-time setup)
docs.text:
Once access is on, the first job is lining your beds up with Ocean Spray's, so uploads match automatically from then on.

  1. Open PUR Transfer → Ocean Spray.
  2. Pick the year — your contract number shows at the top.
  3. For each Blossom bed, choose the matching Ocean Spray bed. Unmapped beds are flagged with a warning.
  4. Tap Auto Match to let Blossom match by name, then fix any it couldn't place.

When no warnings remain, your pesticide use can be uploaded.

docs.title: Agrian
docs.text:
Agrian has its own tab beside Ocean Spray.

Coming with V2, not finished yet

Agrian is in scope for V2, but the section isn't fully connected yet, so the steps haven't been confirmed on a working farm and aren't written up here. If you report through Agrian, use the tab when it goes live and expect this page to be filled in then — it isn't abandoned, just not ready.

docs.title: Work orders
docs.text: A work order is a spray job written down before it happens: the mix, the beds, who is applying it and when. It sits in the Applications ledger alongside finished applications, and it turns into one once the work is recorded.

docs.title: Writing one
docs.text: Tap Applications → New application, then either New pesticide work order or New nutrient work order. You fill it in the same way you'd log an application that had happened — beds, products, rates — except you give it a target date instead of a date applied, and nobody has done the work yet.

docs.title: Spotting one in the ledger
docs.text:
Work-order entries look different from finished applications. Instead of a rate and a target, they show:

Work order #1037 · Target September 11, 2026 · Applicator: Owen Keane Products applied: Drexel Carbaryl 4L · Badge SC · Sil-MATRIX LC · TIDE PPZ+Azoxy · 1 application · 18.47 ac · Open

The date is labelled Target rather than being the date it happened — the job is still ahead of you. If nobody has been assigned yet, the card says No applicator assigned instead of a name.

Two vocabularies for status

The status filter at the top of the ledger offers Requested · Approved · Completed, but the chips on work-order cards read Open, Awaiting approval and Completed. They describe the same journey in slightly different words, so don't be thrown when a card says Open and the filter doesn't.

docs.title: Reading a work order
docs.text: Tap the card to open it.

docs.title: The mix
docs.text:
Each product in the tank is listed with everything the applicator needs:

Shown Means Group FRAC 11, FRAC 3 The resistance group — for rotating chemistry 6.45 fl oz/ac The rate 32.44 fl oz for 5.03 ac The total to mix, already worked out REI 12 h Restricted-entry interval PHI 45 d Pre-harvest interval

docs.title: The beds
docs.text:
Under ON 4 BEDS every bed on the order is listed with its acreage, its variety and the state of that line — Planned until it's recorded.

A line at the bottom tells you how many of them can be drawn on the Map: "2 of 4 beds on this order have a shape — all 4 are in the beds panel." Beds without a boundary still appear on the order and still get sprayed; they just can't be shaded on the map.

docs.title: Restrictions for this mix
docs.text:
This is the part worth reading twice. When several products go on together, Blossom works out the restriction that covers the whole treated area and states it plainly:

Binding hold: REI 48 h — Badge SC · do not enter without PPE until Sun, Sep 13, 2026

Earliest harvest: Mon, Oct 26, 2026 — longest PHI is 45 d (TIDE PPZ+Azoxy).

Two rules are doing the work, and How this is worked out spells them out:

  • The longest REI governs a co-application (40 CFR Part 170). One re-entry clock covers everything once the products go on together — you cannot treat the 4-hour product as 4 hours because it shared a tank with a 48-hour one.
  • The longest PHI sets the earliest harvest, and the REI is used instead if it happens to run longer.

The label governs, always

A label may set its own restriction for a specific tank-mix combination, and that provision wins for that combination. Blossom's figure is a calculation from the products you entered — it is a check on your reading of the labels, never a replacement for it.

docs.title: Recording the work
docs.text:
When the job is done, tap Record completion.

  1. Date Completed — required.
  2. Completed By — pick the applicator. The list shows certification numbers, so Owen Keane (MA-14542) rather than just a name.
  3. # Injections, Temp (°F) and Wind (MPH) if you're recording them.
  4. Weather Conditions — tick what applied: Sunny · P Cloudy · Clear · Cloudy · OVC · Foggy · Calm · Rain · Lt Breeze · Drizzle.
  5. Under Beds to mark complete, tick each bed that was actually applied on this date. Each one shows its product and acreage.
  6. Tap Complete Work Order.

You can finish an order in stages

The bed list is a set of tick boxes precisely because a spray often runs over more than one day. Tick only the beds you did, save, and come back for the rest — the order tracks it as Lines: 2 of 4 done until everything is in. A Target date that has passed is flagged overdue, so a half-finished order won't quietly disappear.

docs.title: Beds
docs.text:
Your beds are the foundation of everything in Blossom — tests, applications, water and harvest all attach to a bed. Tap Beds in the sidebar.

The screen has four tabs:

Tab What it's for Beds Every bed for the season, grouped by block Blocks The blocks those beds are grouped into Management Units Groupings used for nutrient management and compliance Vines Sanding, pruning and mowing, bed by bed

  • Managing Your Beds

    View and search your beds, open a bed's details, and add a new one.

    Open

  • Blocks & Management Units

    The two ways Blossom groups beds, and what each one is for.

    Open

  • Vines — sanding, pruning & mowing

    Record vine care and see when each bed was last done.

    Open

Beds belong to a season

The year selector sits at the bottom-left, next to your farm name. Switching years shows that season's beds, so check you're on the right year before adding or editing anything.

docs.title: Blocks & Management Units
docs.text:
Blossom groups your beds two ways, and they do different jobs:

  • Blocks group beds by where they are — beds that sit together, or share a pump or a flood. This is the grouping you see on the Beds tab and when picking beds for a job.
  • Management units group beds for nutrient management and compliance reporting, including the NRCS 590 reports.

A bed belongs to exactly one block. Management units are set up separately and can cover whichever beds you need.

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text:
1. Tap Beds in the sidebar, then the Blocks tab.
  2. Each card shows the block's name, how many beds it holds, and its total acreage — Block A · 8 beds · 25.1 ac.

From here you can:

  • Add Block — create a new one.
  • Filter — narrow the list.
  • Reorder — change the order blocks appear in, which also sets the order beds are listed on the Beds tab.

Put blocks in walking order

Because Reorder drives the order beds appear everywhere else, it's worth arranging blocks the way your crew actually works round the marsh. It makes every bed picker faster for the rest of the season.

A bed's block is set on the bed itself — see Managing Your Beds.

docs.title: Management units
docs.text:
1. Tap Beds in the sidebar, then the Management Units tab.
  2. Search by name or bed to find an existing unit.
  3. Tap Add Unit to create one: name it, then pick the beds it covers.

Management units are what your nutrient and compliance reports are broken out by — including (NRCS 590) Management Units and the 5 Year Nutrient Management Summary under Reports.

Nothing here yet?

A season with no units shows "No management units recorded for 2026." Management units are per season, so a new year starts empty until you set them up.

docs.title: Managing Your Beds
docs.text: Everything else in Blossom hangs off a bed — a test, a spray, a sprinkler run, a harvest ticket all point back to one. This page covers finding your beds, reading a bed's record, and adding a new one.

docs.title: Finding a bed
docs.text:
1. Tap Beds in the sidebar.
  2. Beds are grouped under their block — Block A, Block B, and so on.
  3. Each tile shows the bed name, a variety chip, and its acres — for example A1 · MQ · 3.24 ac.
  4. Use Search beds by name or code to jump straight to one, or Filter to narrow the list.

Grouped by block, not by management unit

If you're coming from the old Blossom, this is the change you'll notice first: the Beds screen now groups by block. Management units have moved to their own tab.

docs.title: Reading a bed
docs.text:
Tap any bed to open it. The bed opens on General, with tabs across the top:

Tab What's there General Acreage, variety, block, planting and harvest details Tests Soil and tissue results for this bed Applications Pesticide and nutrient applications that included it Water Sprinkler and flood events Vines Sanding, pruning and mowing history Actions Edit, and the other things you can do to the bed

Near the top you'll see the bed's acreage split three ways — productive, inactive, and total — with Edit acreage beside it. Below that sit the variety, block, year planted, production status, bed status, harvest unit and harvest method.

No shape yet?

A bed with no boundary drawn shows "No mapped shape for this bed." Shapes come from the Map, not from this screen.

docs.title: Adding a bed
docs.text:
1. On the Beds tab, tap Add Bed.
  2. Fill in the BED section:
    • Name — required. It appears on maps, work orders and harvest tickets, so use the name your crew already says out loud.
    • Acres — required. Total surface, water included.
    • Bed block — required. Pick from your existing blocks; each one shows how many beds it already holds.
    • Year planted — leave it at this season and the bed is age 0.
    • Production status — Process, New, Out or Fresh.
    • Bed status — Active, or Inactive (year off) for a bed taking a season off with no active acres.
    • EU designation — whether this season's fruit from the bog is grown for the EU market. Leave it Not set if it doesn't apply.
  3. Pick a VARIETY — required.
  4. SPRINKLERS takes line spacing and head spacing, if you track them.
  5. ADVANCED holds the optional extras: alias, inactive acres, harvest unit, harvest method and notes.
  6. Tap Add bed — or Save & add another if you're entering several in one sitting.

Mowed acres live under Advanced

If a bed is down for a year, set Bed status to Inactive (year off) and put the mowed acreage in ADVANCED ▸ inactive acres.

docs.title: Vines — sanding, pruning & mowing
docs.text: The Vines tab is where vine care lives: sanding, pruning and mowing, all in one place, with a running record of when each bed was last done.

docs.title: Seeing what was done, and when
docs.text:
1. Tap Beds in the sidebar, then the Vines tab.
  2. Use the filters to narrow to All, Sanding, Pruning or Mowing.
  3. Under Last done, a count tells you how many beds you are looking at — 150 beds, oldest first. Each tile shows the date, the kind of work, and how long ago it was: R3 · Sanded · Jan 2024 · 2 years ago.
  4. Narrow by age with Any time · 1+ years ago · 2+ years ago · 3+ years ago · 5+ years ago, or search for a single bed by name.

It is built to be a worklist

The list is sorted oldest first, and the age filters do the rest: choose 3+ years ago and you have exactly the beds overdue for sanding, without reading a single date.

Beds never done sit at the bottom — let the filter find them

Beds with no vine work on record show a dash instead of a date, and in the unfiltered list they sit at the bottom, not the top. That is the opposite of where you would look for the most overdue beds, so they are easy to miss.

The age filter solves it. Choose 3+ years ago and the count tells you what you are dealing with — 16 of 150 shown — and every one of those sixteen is a bed with nothing on record at all. That is your worklist.

docs.title: Recording vine work
docs.text:
Log offers all three jobs:

  • Log sanding event
  • Log pruning event
  • Log mowing event

Sanding is the one with a depth; the others record what was done and where.

docs.title: Recording a sanding event
docs.text:
1. On the Vines tab, tap Log → Log sanding event.
  2. Fill in WHEN & DEPTH:
    • Date — required.
    • Depth (inches) — required.
  3. Under BEDS, choose every bed that got sanded. One event can cover as many beds as you sanded that day, so there's no need to log them one at a time.
  4. Add NOTES if there's anything worth remembering.
  5. Tap Add.

The event then shows against each bed you picked, both here and on that bed's Vines tab.

One event, many beds

Record the day's work as a single event across all the beds it covered, rather than one event per bed. The per-bed history is built for you.

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text: The season laid out by date — what's scheduled, what's been done, and your own notes alongside. Tap Calendar in the sidebar.

docs.title: Four ways to look at it
docs.text:
Switch between Year, Month, Week and Day at the top. The year selector sits beside them, so you can look back at a past season the same way.

  • Year for the shape of a season at a glance.
  • Month for planning the weeks ahead.
  • Week and Day for what's actually happening now.

docs.title: Reading a day
docs.text:
Everything on the calendar names itself in the same shorthand — what, then how much:

Looks like Is Ridomil Gold SL (7 beds) An application — the product and how many beds Fruit rot (#1037) A work order — its target and number COOLING (17 beds) · FROST (8 beds) · DRY (9 beds) A water event — the reason in capitals

A busy day is truncated with +3 more; tap the day to see all of it.

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
Once the season has loaded, a Filter row appears with a chip for each kind of thing actually on your calendar — Work Order · Pesticide · Sprinkler Event.

The chips are built from your data

You only ever see chips for things this farm records, so the row is short and there is nothing to wade through. If a kind you expected isn't offered, nothing of that kind is on the calendar for this season.

docs.title: Adding a note
docs.text:
Tap Add note to put something on the calendar that isn't an application, an event or a job — a delivery window, a contractor's visit, when the bees arrive.

The calendar fills itself in

Applications, water events and scheduled work appear here automatically as you record them elsewhere. You don't maintain the calendar; you read it. Notes are for the things Blossom has no other place for.

Give it a moment on a big farm

A season's worth of events takes a few seconds to gather — you'll see "Loading this season's events…" while it does.

docs.text:
